programs.name: Motor City Match
programs.eligibility_summary_as_published: Serves new and informal businesses in Detroit across stages from business planning through permanent space; Round 33 is for "new brick-and-mortar Detroit businesses" (DEGC, 2026-07-28 post). Five service tracks; property listings limited to vacant commercial property in the city.
programs.award_range: Round 33: $315,000 total, average grant about $50,000 (DEGC post); "$21 Million in grants awarded" to date (program site)
programs.verification_note: motorcitymatch.com read 2026-09-21 (Round 33 window Sept 1 - Oct 1, 2026; selection Oct 1 - Dec 31, 2026; applicants notified by Dec 31, 2026). Amounts from degc.org post 'Detroit to award more than $1 million in grants to local entrepreneurs' (posted 2026-07-28, updated 2026-08-07). Apply: https://www.motorcitymatch.com/apply/
limitations: Eligibility is determined by the administrator; this app never states that a user qualifies.

programs.name: Motor City Re-Store (Restore Track of Motor City Match)
programs.eligibility_summary_as_published: "Detroit-based business owners (and their landlords) actively operating in a commercial storefront in the City of Detroit for at least 1-year"; now branded as the Restore Track of Motor City Match.
programs.award_range: Grants "can cover 50% of total project costs" "up to $25,000" (motorcityre-store.com); design services funded up to $10,000; groups of businesses eligible for 75% matching grants (program guidelines as published)
programs.geography_rule: Commercial storefront in the City of Detroit
programs.verification_note: motorcityre-store.com read 2026-09-21; it directs applicants to https://www.motorcitymatch.com/restore-track/. No 2026 round dates were published on the page read today; PRD notes a quarterly cycle (up to $500K per quarter). Treat the window as unknown until a dated round page is read.
limitations: Eligibility is determined by the administrator; this app never states that a user qualifies.

programs.name: Green Grocer Project

Round 4 targeted "small-format grocery stores" and "independent grocers and food retailers" (DEGC post).
programs.award_range: Round 4: $100,000 total, grants up to $25,000 each (DEGC post 2026-07-28)
programs.geography_rule: Business address within the City of Detroit
programs.verification_note: degc.org/green-grocer-project read 2026-09-21 (eligibility text); round dates and amounts from the degc.org 2026-07-28 post. The Round 4 window has closed; next window unknown.

programs.name: Detroit Startup Fund
programs.administrator: Detroit Economic Growth Corporation (DEGC) with the City of Detroit
programs.eligibility_summary_as_published: "Detroit-based startup or founder building in Detroit" established no more than 10 years ago; scalable, venture-backable company; commitment to City certification as a Detroit-based business and to sharing progress and outcome data with DEGC and the City (DEGC launch post). Round 3 targets "technology startups with exponentially scalable business models".
programs.award_range: Round 3: $300,000 total; seed grants of $15,000 and scale grants of $50,000
programs.geography_rule: Detroit-based startup or founder building in Detroit

programs.name: Detroit Business Certification (CRIO Detroit Business Opportunity Program)
programs.administrator: City of Detroit Civil Rights, Inclusion & Opportunity Department (CRIO)
programs.eligibility_summary_as_published: CRIO "processes applications, maintains an online register, and annually certifies and recertifies Detroit Based Businesses (DBB), Detroit Headquartered Businesses (DHB), Detroit Resident Businesses (DRB), Detroit Small Businesses (DSB), Detroit Based Micro Businesses (DBMB), Detroit Start-Ups (DSU), Minority-Owned Business Enterprises (MBE), and Woman-Owned Business Enterprises (WBE). Depending on the certification, businesses qualify for the following benefits: appreciation events, networking and capacity building opportunities, equalization credits, and visibility on the register." (City register dataset description). Most certifications require one taxable year in business; Start-Up, WBE and MBE are the exceptions.
programs.geography_rule: Detroit-based, -headquartered, -resident or -small business definitions per certification type
programs.verification_note: detroitmi.gov served a Cloudflare bot challenge on 2026-09-21 (not bypassed). The eight certification types are quoted from the City's Detroit Business Certification Register feature-service description (services2.arcgis.com, read 2026-09-21). The one-taxable-year rule and its exceptions (Start-Up, WBE, MBE) are as recorded in docs/product/PRD.md, verified by Gregory on 2026-09-21; re-read the CRIO page manually before display.

details.one_taxable_year_rule: Most certifications require one taxable year in business.

limitations: Eligibility is determined by the administrator; this app never states that a user qualifies.
